intro: The Indian Journalist visa is for journalists, photographers and news crews visiting India professionally. Journalism isn’t allowed on an e-Visa, so you need this visa.
cardText: For journalists, photographers and news crews working in India.

purposes.text: Covering news or features in India.

rules.title: Your passport goes to the visa centre
rules.text: Regular visas are stuck into your passport, so you’ll need to submit it at the Indian visa application centre. Don’t book travel you can’t change until it’s back.

rules.title: Allow more time
rules.text: Regular visas take longer than e-Visas, and much longer for people of Pakistani origin. Apply as early as you can.

rules.title: The form must be exact
rules.text: Any mismatch between your form, passport and documents can delay or refuse the application. We check everything line by line.

rules.title: Arrive anywhere
rules.text: Unlike e-Visas, regular visas can be used at any immigration checkpoint in India.

boxText: Feature films, series and adverts use the e-Film visa.

sections.heading: Who needs an Indian Journalist visa?
sections.text: Professional journalists and media crews can’t use the e-Visa, even for a short trip. Apply early: journalist applications go through extra checks.

sections.heading: Documents for an Indian Journalist visa
sections.text: Your passport, a recent photo, proof of your UK address, a letter from your media organisation confirming your role and assignment, and details of where you’ll go and what you’ll cover. Freelancers should bring letters from the outlets commissioning the work.

sections.heading: How long does it take?
sections.text: Journalist applications go through extra checks, so allow several weeks before you travel. Apply as early as you can and don’t book fixed travel until your Indian Journalist visa is approved.

faqs.q: Can I go to India on holiday if I’m a journalist?
faqs.a: Tell us about your work first. Rules for media professionals are stricter, and we’ll advise on the right visa.

faqs.q: Can I apply myself instead of using you?
faqs.a: Yes. You can apply on the official website, indianvisaonline.gov.in, and pay only the government fee. People use us when they want a person to check their eligibility, fix their photo and documents, and handle the form for them so nothing goes wrong.

faqs.q: Do freelance journalists need an Indian Journalist visa?
faqs.a: Yes, if you’re travelling to report or film for the media. Letters from the outlets commissioning your work help your application.

faqs.q: Can a journalist go to India on an e-Visa?
faqs.a: Not for journalism. Professional media work needs an Indian Journalist visa.
